sceneAlt: A small café with nobody in it: a ceiling fan and a lamp above, a clock on the back wall, a long counter with a coffee machine, a toaster, a sink, a kettle, a pretzel, a cake, a cash register and a telephone, and a drinks fridge behind it. On the left a bench, a sofa and an umbrella stand; in the middle a bar stool and a round table set with a teapot, a cup and a croissant; on the right a bin.
help.hook: An empty café before opening time: tap each thing in the picture, then give it its article.
help.intro: A picture hunt instead of a deck: one small, cosy café before opening time, with a counter and nobody in it with 32 things to find in it, every one an everyday noun — der Tresen, die Kaffeemaschine, das Milchkännchen, the cake on the counter and the croissant on the table. The prompt asks a question like Wo ist der Teppich? and you tap the object in the picture. A tap on the wrong object tells you what you hit and you keep looking; after three misses the right one is shown. Each find shows its label, coloured by its gender, then leaves a small tick in that colour, so you can see what you have already found. Once you have passed a run, the hunt gets harder: the prompt hides the article (Wo ist ___ Kaffeemaschine?), and after the find you pick der, die or das yourself. No object is asked twice in the same run.
help.tips[0].title: -chen makes every word neuter
help.tips[0].text: The ending -chen (and -lein) makes a thing small, and it always makes it das, whatever the word was before. Die Kanne is a big jug; the little milk jug on the table is das Milchkännchen. The vowel often gets an umlaut too: Kanne → Kännchen.
help.tips[0].check.why: Every noun in -chen is neuter, even though die Kanne is feminine.
help.tips[1].title: Devices in -er are masculine — but watch die Maschine
help.tips[1].text: A device named with -er, the thing that does the job, is der: der Toaster, der Wasserkocher, der Mülleimer is the odd one out that is masculine without being a machine. Do not let the coffee fool you: die Kaffeemaschine takes its article from die Maschine.
help.tips[1].check.why: Devices in -er are masculine: der Toaster, der Wasserkocher.
help.tips[2].title: The front part never decides
help.tips[2].text: Das Wasser is neuter, but at the front of a word it changes nothing: der Wasserkocher (der Kocher), der Wasserhahn (der Hahn). The same trick works all over this room: die Wanduhr (die Uhr), der Regenschirm (der Schirm), der Schirmständer (der Ständer).
help.tips[2].check.why: The last part is der Ständer, so the compound is der Schirmständer.
help.remember[0]: Every -chen word is das: das Milchkännchen, even though die Kanne is feminine.
help.remember[1]: Devices in -er are der: der Toaster, der Wasserkocher.
help.remember[2]: The counter in a café is der Tresen; the plural is die Tresen, unchanged.
